resources.string: Lets Kiri lock the screen when you choose a gesture for it, such as a double tap on the home screen. Kiri does not read anything on the screen.
Android asks for Kiri to be turned on in Accessibility before it can lock the screen
This build of Kiri, the one from Google Play, has no accessibility service, so no gesture can lock the screen here. The APK from GitHub can.
For a gesture to lock the screen, such as a double tap on the home screen, Kiri uses Android\'s accessibility service. It is the only way Android gives an app to lock the screen.
It only locks the screen, and only when you make the gesture you chose.
It reads nothing on the screen, does not see what you type, receives nothing from other apps, and collects or sends no data.
Choose another action for the gesture: the service then leaves Android’s list.
Opens Android\'s Accessibility, where you turn Kiri on
The gesture stays as it was
The gesture does not lock the screen until you allow it
